name: Reception — Scheduling
description: Review-by-default scheduling reception (a booking front-door). A visitor picks a slot and the booking lands a pending record; a review-then-approve workflow holds the materialize operation at the Gateway gate, where you approve (editing the slot time / details first) or reject. Materializes a booking in your local warehouse — a mutable business record that owns its own slot and lifecycle (confirmed / completed / no_show / cancelled). A booking is never written to your calendar: the calendar is personal, a booking is business (D-210 A.2). Scheduling never auto-books (D-173 I-7).

operations.description: Materialize a reviewed reservation into a BOOKING row (the review-then-approve projection). ⛔ It does NOT create a calendar event and never has since D-210 A.2: booking ⟂ calendar, so the booking carries its own slot_start_at / slot_end_at and is the only artifact. Approval-required: the Gateway gate holds it pending so the owner reviews + edits the slot start / details before it runs, and the EDITED value is what is minted — the reservation row keeps what the visitor originally ASKED, this records what was AGREED. A past-slot booking is never materialized (I-7) — the projection refuses once the slot is in the past. Set notify_visitor to tell the visitor their booking is confirmed; it is off unless the owner turns it on for this approval, and it needs a send-capable sender configured on the scheduling link. The `https://reception.local` base url (surfaces_seed) is a LOCAL-DISPATCH sentinel, not a reachable endpoint — on approve-resume the ingredient executor routes this op to the in-process `reception-materialize` kernel ingredient (runReceptionProjection), so the materialize never makes an HTTP call (D-173 I-2 / P1-dispatch).

editable_args.label: Tell the visitor their booking is confirmed
